draft.title: Intermolecular forces
card: Intermolecular forces are attractions between separate molecules. They are much weaker than the covalent bonds inside each molecule.
Dispersion forces
act between all molecules. They are stronger in larger molecules, which have more electrons.
Dipole-dipole forces
act between polar molecules, where the slightly positive end of one molecule attracts the slightly negative end of another.
Hydrogen bonds

are a strong type of dipole-dipole force. They form when hydrogen is bonded to nitrogen, oxygen or fluorine, and is attracted to such an atom in a neighbouring molecule. When a molecular substance boils, the forces between molecules are overcome, not the bonds inside them. Stronger forces mean a higher boiling point.
draft.remember: Boiling overcomes the forces between molecules. The stronger they are, the higher the boiling point.

a.q: Water boils at a much higher temperature than hydrogen sulfide, which has similar sized molecules. Which is the best explanation?
opts: Water molecules form hydrogen bonds with each other
Water has stronger covalent bonds inside its molecules
Water molecules have far more electrons than H2S ones
Water is the only one that has dispersion forces
a.why: Hydrogen is bonded to oxygen in water, so water molecules form hydrogen bonds, which are stronger than the other forces here. Boiling does not break the covalent bonds inside molecules, so stronger covalent bonds would not explain it.
a.clue: Think about which forces are overcome when water boils.

b.q: Methane (CH4) has a lower boiling point than ethane (C2H6). Both are non-polar molecules. Which is the best reason?
opts: Ethane has stronger dispersion forces, with more electrons
Ethane has hydrogen bonds between its molecules
Ethane has dipole-dipole forces because it is polar
Ethane has stronger covalent bonds between its atoms
b.why: Both molecules are non-polar, so only dispersion forces act. Ethane is larger with more electrons, so its dispersion forces are stronger and it boils at a higher temperature. Covalent bonds are not broken when a molecular substance boils.
b.clue: Both are non-polar, so which force is left, and what makes it stronger?

a.best: Water molecules form hydrogen bonds with each other

b.best: Ethane has stronger dispersion forces, with more electrons

problems.detail: The stem says H2S has 'similar sized molecules' to water, but H2S molecules are larger, with 18 electrons against water's 10 (molar mass 34 vs 18). This matters because dispersion forces depend on size: H2S would be expected to boil higher, which makes water's high boiling point the striking point. Better: 'which is a larger molecule with more electrons'.
